messages:
Alex K: Hey folks — quick onboarding question. I just added my spouse as a dependent in the benefits portal. Two quick things: 1) Does adding a spouse change my federal/state tax withholding automatically? 2) We want to switch to the commuter pre-tax monthly pass — is that handled in the same benefits flow or do I need payroll to enable it? Thanks!

Jordan (People Ops): Welcome aboard Alex! :wave: Short answers: health dependent enrollments don’t usually change your W-4 automatically, and commuter pre-tax is separate. I’ll loop in payroll to confirm the steps and any tax implications.

Mona S (Payroll): Hi Alex — congrats and thanks for checking. For steps: 1) If you added your spouse under Life Events in Workday/Benefits, that just enrolls them for coverage. It won’t change your W-4. If you want to change withholding, update your W-4 in Payroll > Tax Forms.

Mona S (Payroll): 2) Commuter pre-tax: we use the Transit/Commuter enrollment in the Benefits portal. Quick checklist:
```
- Go to Benefits Portal > Supplemental Benefits
- Select "Commuter / Transit"
- Choose monthly pass or pre-tax deduction amount
- Submit and confirm payroll deduction appears on next paystub
```

Mona S (Payroll): Note: commuter deductions are pre-tax and will reduce taxable wages, but they don’t alter your W-4 allowances. If you want an estimate of take-home after both changes, I can run a mock payroll calc for you.

Alex K: Awesome — could you run that mock calc? Also, my spouse has employer coverage too; any conflict if we enroll both places?

Mona S (Payroll): You can be double-enrolled but usually one plan is primary and the other secondary. That’s fine from our side. If your spouse’s employer is primary, coordination of benefits happens at claim time. We don’t need paperwork to enroll both, but if you want the company subsidy split or premium deductions corrected, send the spouse’s employer name and policy ID and I’ll note it.

Payroll Bot: Ticket #PH-11327 created for Alex K — Payroll will follow up in the thread with the mock estimate. Link: https://internal.redwood/payroll/tickets/PH-11327

Ryan P: Congrats Alex! If you need help with benefits portal MFA, ping me — took me a sec to find the transit tab. :slightly_smiling_face:

Mona S (Payroll): @Alex K I ran a quick estimate — with spouse on coverage and $120/month commuter pre-tax, your taxable wages reduce by ~$1,440 annually from commuter deductions; premium splits depend on plan tier. I’ll DM the detailed mock paystub numbers (need last 4 of your SSN & preferred state for exact calc).

Alex K: Thanks Mona — I’ll DM the details. Jordan — should I mark this as a life event for benefits audit?

Jordan (People Ops): Yes please mark Life Event in the portal if you haven’t already and attach a copy of the marriage certificate (or domestic partnership docs). I’ll add a note to your onboarding checklist.

Mona S (Payroll): Follow-up: If anyone else reading wants the commuter quick steps, I copied them to #onboarding-resources.

Alex K: Got it, thanks everyone!

Jordan (People Ops): Thanks — closing the thread once payroll confirms DM. :white_check_mark:
